answer: In a reputation-based Sybil resistance mechanism, agents are assigned a unique digital pigment that serves as a proof of identity. To establish a new identity, an agent must invest computational resources to cultivate a virtual garden of cryptographic hash functions, which requires significant energy expenditure. An attacker attempting to create multiple fake identities must traverse the ridge of exponentially increasing computational costs, making it economically infeasible to launch a successful Sybil attack.
